question.leadin: Answer some questions about the 18th President of the United States.
question.text: Prior to becoming President, Grant served in this war that began in 1846, the year after the United States annexed Texas. This war was ended by the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.
question.clue: The Wilmot Proviso suggested banning slavery in lands gained from this conflict.

swap.text: Marshall was a member of this political party that advocated for a strong central government.
swap.clue: The Coodies were a faction of this party from Maryland.

question.text: Douglass was the only African-American attendee of this event, which was planned by Elizabeth Cady Stanton. This event culminated in the Declaration of Sentiments.
question.clue: This event led to the adoption of 11 resolutions, including a ninth one supported by Frederick Douglass that called for the "elective franchise."

swap.text: The shortcomings of the Articles of Confederation were made widely apparent when the federal government couldn't fund an army to put down this 1786 uprising in Massachusetts. Instead, Benjamin Lincoln took a private collection and led a militia to end this rebellion.
swap.clue: In the end, only Charles Rose and John Bly were hanged, after this event had petered out with a final conflict at Egremont.

question.leadin: Decades before becoming President, this man wrote the Braintree Instructions to oppose the Stamp Act.
question.text: Name this second President of the United States.
question.answerHtml: John Adams [prompt on Adams; do not accept “John Quincy Adams”]
question.clue: In a letter, this man's wife urged him to "remember the Ladies" in making laws.

swap.text: Adams' appointment of "Midnight Judges" sparked this case. Charles Lee represented the plaintiff in this case, in which John Marshall declared the Judiciary Act of 1789 unconstitutional.
swap.clue: The namesake of this case had been appointed justice of the peace in the District of Columbia, as one of John Adams' "Midnight Judges."

question.text: The earthquakes may have been felt as far away as Washington, D.C., where this president was preparing for the War of 1812. This shortest president drafted the Bill of Rights and succeeded Thomas Jefferson.
question.clue: This man wrote the original version of the 27th Amendment, and as president this man temporarily governed from Brookeville, Maryland after the Battle of Bladensburg.

swap.leadin: Horace Greeley's book The American Conflict was the first to claim that this politician exclaimed "John Marshall has made his decision; now let him enforce it!"
swap.text: Name this president who disregarded the Supreme Court's ruling in Worcester v. Georgia. A policy enacted by this president was continued by the signing of the Treaty of New Echota under his successor.
swap.clue: This victor at the Battle of New Orleans implemented the rotation in office system and issued the Specie Circular.

question.leadin: Name these Chief Justices of the Supreme Court from some decisions they wrote.
question.text: Marbury v. Madison, Barron v. Baltimore, McCulloch v. Maryland
question.clue: In another decision, this person wrote "The power to tax is the power to destroy."

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the controversial Orders in Council.
swap.text: James Madison once said that he would have delayed declaring this war with Great Britain if he had known that the Orders in Council had been rescinded. The Battle of New Orleans was fought after the peace treaty ending this war was signed.
swap.clue: The defeat of the Guerriere by the Constitution was a significant ship action in this war, during which an attack at Beaver Dams failed due to the British being warned by Laura Secord.

question.leadin: Thinking of law school? If so, you might find it helpful to answer some questions about American legal precedent.
question.text: This power, granted to the Supreme Court in Marbury v. Madison, allows courts to strike down laws that judges deem unconstitutional.
question.clue: The appointment of "midnight justices" led to the case which instituted this practice.

swap.leadin: The first of these conflicts began when a flag pole in front of the American consulate in Tripoli was chopped down.
swap.text: Give the collective names for these two conflicts, sometimes dubbed the Algerian and Tripolitan wars, fought between the United States and several North African States.
swap.answerHtml: Barbary Wars [accept Barbary Coast Wars or Barbary Pirates Wars]
swap.clue: Another began with the capture of the Meshuda at the Battle of Cape Gata after a declaration of war by Umar ben Muhammed.

question.leadin: In response to these documents, their target slandered his opponent by accusing him of pimping out a young American girl to the Tsar of Russia.
question.text: Name these pamphlets that contained vicious personal attacks accusing one candidate of consuming the corpses of defeated Native Americans while slandering his wife over the charge of alleged bigamy during the 1828 election.
question.clue: This documents released by Philadelphia news editor John Binns during the election of 1828.

swap.leadin: This legislation inspired a political cartoon where the pants of a man holding a barrel are bitten by a turtle named "O-Grab-Me."
swap.text: Name this 1807 act signed by Thomas Jefferson, which limited trade with France and Great Britain after the Chesapeake-Leopard Affair.
swap.clue: In a political cartoon, this act was depicted as a turtle biting a man who says, "Oh! This cursed Ograbme!"

question.leadin: The only indentured servant ever to serve in Congress, Matthew Lyon, was the first person convicted under this act.
question.text: Name this act. Samuel Chase and James Callendar threatened to beat and kill each other after Chase imprisoned Callender under this act.
question.clue: While circuit riding, Samuel Chase drew the ire of Republicans for presiding over the prosecution of many Republicans under this law. James Callender was jailed under this law.

swap.leadin: In this Supreme Court case, Chief Justice John Marshall put forth his principle that "the power to tax involves the power to destroy."
swap.text: Name this Supreme Court case, which found that Congress had authority to charter the Second Bank of the United States, and that a certain state's taxation of the bank was a form of unconstitutional interference.
swap.clue: The representative of the namesake Mid-Atlantic state in this case, which sought to impose a tax on a federal institution, argued that the "Constitution is silent on the subject of banks."

question.leadin: Answer the following about what happened after the Battle of the Alamo.
question.text: This two-word term is used to describe the two months in early 1836 after the fall of the Alamo, when native Texans fled from their homes, hastily abandoning settlements like Washington-on-the-Brazos in fear of Santa Anna's army.
question.clue: Houston's victory at San Jacinto came after this desperate campaign, during which news of the massacres at the Alamo and Goliad caused the provisional government of Texas to flee from Santa Anna's advancing army.

swap.text: This 1795 treaty was the first of many signed by Spain and the United States over the status of Florida. It extended the Florida/Georgia border all the way to the Mississippi River.
swap.clue: In part, it guaranteed free navigation of the Mississippi and the right of deposit in New Orleans for 3 years.

question.leadin: According to legend, a horse-drawn railcar outraced this machine after it lost a blower belt.
question.text: Name this steam locomotive designed by Peter Cooper, the first in the US to operate on common carrier rails.
question.clue: This steam locomotive constructed by Peter Cooper in 1829 for use in railroad transportation.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about taverns in early American history.
swap.text: This widowed wife of John Timberlake became infamous for telling jokes at taverns across Washington D.C., but is more infamous for causing the Petticoat Affair by marrying Andrew Jackson's Secretary of War.
swap.clue: Though once a supporter and friend of Andrew Jackson, their relation was severed when Calhoun joined his wife and other cabinet members in socially ostracizing this wife of the secretary of war for committing adultery.
